evidence: 0099 (offline audit patient check; OFFLINE-CONTRACT.md amendment A10 item 1, after the review of hid-system#131, under the owner decisions D1-D15 of 2026-10-29; signed by D-Eminence in chat on 2026-10-30: Approve, in reply to the request to approve 0099) is additive. The only caller is the EHR API's offline audit ingest (C2, from #131, live since 2026-10-30), which looks for the function on every request naming a patient: without it C2 answers 503 OFFLINE_AUDIT_UNAVAILABLE and writes nothing; with it, events for patients the caller never held a qualifying grant for are refused as PATIENT_NOT_FOUND. No other answer changes. No table, column, index, policy, trigger or existing function changes: pg_dump --schema-only of a 0098 database before and after the upgrade differs only by the new function, its owner, its comment, its REVOKE from PUBLIC and its GRANT to hid_ehr_runtime. One new function, ehr.offline_audit_patient_allowed(requested_patient_id uuid) returns boolean: LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, not STRICT, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp (every name in the body qualified), owned by ehr.context_allows's owner (the applier, or that owner when the applier is a member that inherits it and may SET ROLE to it). It is true when identity.consent_grants holds a row with that patient_id whose account_id, membership_id and facility_id equal platform.current_account_id(), platform.current_membership_id() and platform.current_facility_id(), with scope read_records or write_records, not break_glass, migration_hold_reason null and starts_at <= now(). Status, revoked_at and expires_at are ignored on purpose (a late-synced offline read stays accepted; A10: expired or revoked grants still count); break-glass is excluded by scope and by flag (owner decision D5: break-glass records are never written to a device; a legacy row may carry one without the other); a null argument, a missing patient, another membership, facility or account, a held or not yet started grant, a disabled account and an empty request context answer false. EXECUTE to hid_ehr_runtime only, in the migration (when the role exists) and in runtime-grants.sql's EHR execute block; revoked from PUBLIC (also in runtime-grants.sql's security-definer revoke list); no grant to any other runtime and no table privilege for any runtime. The sealed demo (0098) is untouched: no 0098 object is read or changed, and grants obey its pair rule, so a demo session answers true only for demo patients; the sealed-demo suite passes after the upgrade. Preconditions (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501 with nothing applied): 0001-0098 applied (0098's table and seal trigger among the objects checked); not applied yet (applying the file again answers '0099: already applied'; the runner reports 0 pending); the md5 of the five bodies relied on (platform.current_actor_subject, current_account_id, current_membership_id, current_facility_id, auth.account_id_for_subject); the types and NOT NULLs of the eight columns read; consent_grants_scope_check and consent_grants_check3; the applier's and owner's privileges, never through a superuser's bypass. Post-checks pin the function's attributes and its exact ACL. Locks, measured with pg_locks before commit on a 0098 copy: ACCESS SHARE on identity.consent_grants (the SQL body's validation; none with check_function_bodies off), SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the new function (its comment), ACCESS SHARE on schema ehr and on the role hid_ehr_runtime (the grant), ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the session's own temporary schema (the precondition helper), the catalogs' own locks; no other application relation and no existing function. A session holding ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.consent_grants did not delay the apply (runner 0.4 s, applied); a write took its lock with NOWAIT while the migration's transaction was open; behind a held ACCESS EXCLUSIVE the runner stopped after 5.15 s with a lock timeout, nothing applied, and applied once the holder ended. Apply time 13-16 ms (the runner's execution_ms). Proved on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 as pgrun: a fresh install of 0001-0099 by the runner before any runtime role existed (owner-only until the role bootstrap, then EXECUTE for hid_ehr_runtime); an upgrade of a 0098 database bootstrapped with 2ec53b0's runtime-grants.sql (the migration itself grants hid_ehr_runtime), after which the bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql changed no privilege (the 1283 non-owner grants in the application schemas identical before and after, and to the fresh install's); all 73 database suites pass on both. A NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner and a member login of it each apply it (owned by the owner either way) and a role that is neither is refused with 42501; four negative copies (a helper body, consent_grants_check3, 0098's seal trigger, the starts_at type) stop with nothing applied. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passes as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (baseline 99 files, integrated 100, dry run rolled back, checksums preserved, migration grants match runtime grants, row-level security unchanged on 185 tables). The new suite services/ehr-api/test/database/offline-audit-patient-allowed.integration.sql passes on the file as committed and fails on 18 mutants: each of the nine where-clause terms dropped in turn, break_glass flipped, a status, expiry or revocation filter added, SECURITY INVOKER, PUBLIC EXECUTE, no search_path, an extra grant to hid_identity_runtime, another owner, STRICT; the migration's own post-checks also refuse SECURITY INVOKER, a missing revoke and a missing search_path written into the file.
